utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff? I was going to tell you to continue, Miss IN Hollis, but I believe that Mr. Wladimiroff has something that he wants to talk about. Yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. There is a small matter I want to raise, that is, next week the Defence will leave for Bosnia. For that reason, I have to prepare some things and, therefore, cannot be always in court. Since Mr. Orie is abroad, I would like to ask the court to permit Miss de Bertodano to address the court, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. who?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano who is a qualified barrister.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: She has been with us many days. That is fine. We will miss you next week, but we understand. Very good. That is acceptable. Did you hear what Judge Stephen said? That is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. MR. SAUD HRNIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, I would remind you that you are still under oath today. Sir, yesterday you testified about five occasions during which you were interrogated and you said that you thought the first interrogation had occurred on a Saturday, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that the second occasion you were taken for interrogation was a Monday, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that the following Monday, two days after the Saturday interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated in your testimony yesterday that you saw your brother's body on a Tuesday, was that the Tuesday after your second interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also testified yesterday about the beatings that you received during your interrogations. Was Zeljko Meakic ever present during any of those beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he ever participate in those beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he do to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was in the interrogation room and there were others beat me. Zeljko Meakic entered and they stopped beating me and he laughed, kicked me with his foot and then turned and left the room and closed the door behind him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yesterday you also testified about an incident during which a man you referred to as "Began" and a few other individuals were beaten. This "Began" that you referred to, was this the same Began you had referred to as being called from room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This beating that you saw in which Began and a few other individuals were beaten, did this occur before or after the incident with Meho Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not be able to say.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the person or persons who beat Began and these other individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see Began again after this beating by Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him when he returned to room 15 again.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see his condition after this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His head was all beaten up. He was all battered. He could not move. His right or left arm, I do not know exactly, was bleeding, bleeding a lot. Somebody brought a tissue to something so we bandaged his arm.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have the technician, please, at the video camera? Sir, yesterday you spoke about certain incidents occurring in certain areas at Omarska. For clarification, I would ask you to again come to the model and point to certain areas as I ask you questions. Again if you would remove your headphones there, come around the corner and use the head phones at the Registrar's desk? Sir, yesterday you indicated that for a portion of your stay at Omarska you were in room 15. At one point you did show the court where that room was. I would ask you again to point to room 15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The witness is pointing to the area that is marked with the numbers B7. There appear to be two smaller enclosures within that room, one marked B8 and one marked B23. If you would look at B8, please, and tell us what was that enclosure?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be given a microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You need to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were large concrete blocks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that room used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was probably when workers came so that they could wash their hands and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The room that is marked B23, the area that is marked B23, what was that used for when you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were shower booths.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This large area with B7 and also containing B8 and B23, this entire area was what was known as room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Also standing there would you please point out for the court the door through which you would enter the hangar and go into room 15? (The witness indicated on the model) Your Honours, if you would note that that is the door that is immediately below B7. You also testified yesterday that you spent a period of time on the pista while you were at Omarska. Could you please point out for the court the area of the pista on which you stayed while you were at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The area that you pointed to, if you will look to the back of that model, you will find a yellow sticky with the letter "W" on it. If you could take that yellow sticky with the letter "W" on it and if you could place it where you would typically be on the pista? If you will look at the building immediately in front of you, the smaller red building, this is the administration building, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could point out to the court the area of the administration building in which you would sleep at night while you were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would note that the witness is pointing to the area with the number A22. Was this the same area that you received your meal each day that you received a meal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this the area you were in the morning that you looked and saw your brother's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you will also look at the pista you will see the front of the restaurant building. If you could come around so you can see the entry side of the restaurant building and if you could point out for the court the window through which you would see detainees being kicked and hit down the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would note that he is pointing to the window on the rounded structure of the building above the number A21. Thank you, sir. If you would please resume your seat at the witness table? Sir, yesterday you testified that you were able to see these people being kicked and falling down these stairs when you were on the pista. You have also indicated that when you were lying on your stomach on the pista you were lying with your head in the direction of the hangar building. Could you tell the court how you are able to see individuals being kicked down these stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, whilst we were on the pista we were mostly in the prone position, but when you lie that way you can turn around, look, look under your arm. It was simply impossible to lie down all the day round without moving. On quite a number of occasions we sat on the pista; it all depended on the guard who was there. So that we could see, or even when we went from the pista to have our lunch, the same thing happened.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, during the testimony yesterday the witness made reference to certain days of the week and to certain dates. At this time I would ask that the court judicially notice the calendar months of April 1992 through December 1992. To assist the court, I have asked that a computer printout of those months of that year be produced. I have copies for the Judges. I have provided a copy to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will mark that as exhibit -- what is the next number? 233. 233 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in that regard I would ask that the Trial Chamber note that 24th May was a Sunday, that the following Tuesday was 26th May, the following Wednesday was 27th May. I would also ask the Chamber to note that 8th June fell on a Monday. Mr. Hrnic, during the time that you were at Omarska did you see Dule Tadic at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On how many occasions did you see Dule Tadic at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that occasion what was Dule Tadic wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing then a uniform, summer camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he doing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what he was doing. I know I saw him on the pista where I was. Whether he was moving or standing still, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he standing up when you saw him, standing upright or sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Standing, standing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your recollection, did he have any weapons in his hands or on his person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your recollection, was he carrying anything in his hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot claim it with certainty, but I think he had something that looked like a file or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "a file", you mean a file such as a binder or a paper type file?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him, do you recall if he had a beard or appeared to be clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you see him? Was this after you had been moved from room 15 to the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him, what position was your body in? Were you sitting, lying, crouching? How were you positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lying down.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Lying down, what, on your stomach, on your back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my stomach.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what direction was your head positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was your face positioned when you saw him? Were you looking down? Was your face turned to the side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that particular moment it was turned to the side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which side, left or right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So as you lay facing the hangar, you are faced to the right, it would have been to the right in the direction of the grass and the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could have the technician come back, please, and, Mr. Hrnic, if I could ask you once again to stand, to move to the model and to indicate to the court where you were when you saw Dule Tadic, and also take the other yellow sticky and indicate where Dule Tadic was when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here, and Dule Tadic was approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, since my view was blocked of your first indication, did you indicate you were in the same position you normally were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you could resume your seat, sir? Thank you. Your Honour, we are going to attempt with this equipment that we have to have a photograph taken that will show these two markers. We have tried it earlier; it turns out fairly well. So we are going to attempt to have that done.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you wish to do that now?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It is going to take some time so if I could continue with the .....

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Those stickies, I do not know whether they have really been pressed down hard or not?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps the technician could check that, to make sure the stickies are in place for the photo? Mr. Hrnic, on the occasion that you saw Dule Tadic, did you see any other persons standing with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the occasion that you saw him, was anything or anyone blocking your view of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see him during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was it a sunny day or a cloudy day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was sunny.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the sunshine interfere with your ability to see him clearly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you recognised Dule Tadic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw him at that moment, if I may put it that way, I kissed the pista, that is, I bed my head down so that he would not see me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you react that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, after that incident that had taken place that other people had talked about, I was simply frightened. I was afraid because he also knew me and in Omarska it usually was that an acquaintance killed his acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, would you please look around the courtroom very carefully and I would ask you that if you see Dule Tadic in the courtroom if you would please point to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us where he is sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is sitting in the back between two policemen and there is a third one standing next to him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could note a proper identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, the gentleman to whom you just pointed, is that the Dule Tadic that you saw in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that the Dule Tadic that you knew from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You told us earlier that from Omarska camp you were taken to Manjaca camp. How were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken by buses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were these civilian or military buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 15th December '92.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken to from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you left Manjaca and went to Karlovac, leaving behind your home and business in your home area, did you do that because you truly wanted to leave or because you felt you had no choice but to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had no other choice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Since the time that you left Bosnia have you been back to opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that because you choose not to go back or because you feel you cannot go back to your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I feel I cannot go back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will there be cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, you told the court yesterday that you knew Dusko Tadic from Kozarac and that you had had karate lessons with him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The karate class that he held in Kozarac contained Muslims like yourself as well as Serbs as well as Croats; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There came a stage when as you were older you went into business and am I right in thinking that you lived outside Kozarac for some time, in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was not clear to me whether you had lived all the time in Kozarac, in Marsala Tita Street, that you indicated on the plan or whether you had also spent time away from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there the whole time. That area was known as Mutnik and I do not know what year the name was changed into Marsala Tita, but the whole time I lived there in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. There came a stage when you said that Muslims were restricted from leaving Kozarac because of the taking over of power in Prijedor and orders were issued that restricted your travelling; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I either did not understand well or -- after May 30th we moved towards Prijedor and I think that we could go to Prijedor up until May 22nd and come back from Prijedor as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I just wanted you to confirm because it was suggested that Muslims were restricted from travelling after the takeover of power in Prijedor at the end of April?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe perhaps counsel was misunderstanding. The transcript, as I have it, the question was that after the takeover did the witness have difficulties travelling between Kozarac and Prijedor. He indicated, yes, he had difficulties. He was not asked, he did not indicate at any point that he could not move between those areas. I am referring to page 1981 of the transcript, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think other witnesses have also dealt with this subject matter, as the court will recall as well.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I believe the objection would be that the question is misleading because it assumes facts in evidence that are not in evidence because that is not what the witness testified to yesterday. Do you want to rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question, if that assists my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. MR. KAY (To the witness): Putting it simply then, Mr. Hrnic, would it be right to say that you could travel to Prijedor after the takeover in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recollect that some Muslims left Kozarac completely during the month of May after that takeover in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For always we still hoped that we eventually will come back to Kozarac and, yes, some people have left Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the attack on Kozarac, some Muslim families left that town, perhaps because they were worried about what was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not know whether you recollect the Arnautovic family? Did you know them, Simo Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or the Memic family? He was the leader of the SDA in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recollect him leaving or his family leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he left only. I know that he left the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told the court that you were on a checkpoint duty up at Rajkovici on the outskirts of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a duty. Yes, I was up there, but I did not have any duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say you did not have a duty. Did you go there of your own free will or did others suggest that you might go there to stand guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went there because I felt I need to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many others were there with you on duty in Rajkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you an exact number. There was at all times about five or six people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told us that you had a rifle, an automatic rifle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did others have weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But some did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The rifle that you had, is it right that it also had a telescopic sight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you telling the truth about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have not told people investigating this case when you were interviewed that you had a telescopic sight on your rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were on duty would it be right to say that you wore a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you wear a beret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- beret is a top part of the uniform, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you wear a beret and by that I mean some form of cap?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had some sort of a hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it green in colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a camouflage one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you wear insignia on your uniform showing a lily, the flower of the lily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you used to wear that uniform around Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were going from one checkpoint to another checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you stand duty on other checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts were those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would go to a checkpoint across from the sawmill, across the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That would be the road leading from the Prijedor/Banja Luka highway into Kozarac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Road Prijedor/Banja Luka towards Mrakovica through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The checkpoint that you were on at Rajkovici, was there another Muslim man who stood duty on there called Sahib Salkanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recognise the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you stand duty then there with a man called Sahib?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sahid?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sahib -- ending with a "B".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not recognise the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the people change regularly on that duty post at Rajkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Change, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were not on duty there, were others standing on duty there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there on my own free will and that was a checkpoint that was in -- that the Kozarac police station was in charge of, together with the people from that area, and those people came to keep company and to stay there with the guards at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You yourself did not work for the police, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, the position that you were standing on at Rajkovici, was that to do with the TO, the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand well. I repeat it to you that there was a police checkpoint that was manned by people from TO, and that were from that area of the town and who stayed there at the checkpoint on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I am talking about the checkpoint at Rajkovici which was usually where you were positioned; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was just wondering from what official body, if there was any, that caused you to become positioned there; were you a member of the TO? Was it because you were in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were organised on our own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "organised", who did that organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No-one organised us. We knew what our fate would be. We could guess it and we tried to organise and have the guards so that we could avoid the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand what you say about that, but when did you obtain your rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that you had an automatic rifle. Had you had that many years or did you buy it in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I bought it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to move now to another matter and that concerns after you had left Kozarac, after the attack on it, and returned on what would have been the Tuesday and with others walked in a column down Marsala Tita Street. First of all, can you tell the court what time it was that you reached the junction of old Kula and Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me again, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not Tuesday; that was Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, that is what I was going to correct. The transcript indicates that when he actually joined the column and marched down to the intersection was Wednesday; Tuesday was when he saw Osman Braco.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged. Yes, that is my mistake. I am talking about the Wednesday, but I think you understand what I am referring to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that it was Wednesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. As to the time, can you help the court with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was at dawn, as soon as the sun came out. I cannot tell you what time it was, but at dawn we left from Besici and whatever it took us to get to the junction in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there many of you moving from Besici down to the junction in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, approximately -- there were many, but there was a column behind me. I was not in front of the column, but maybe 10 metres from the front of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect at all the names of the other people who were in the column with you, who were around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell me who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dzevad Besic. His son was in front with him. They had white flags. They were carrying the flags. His sister and his wife, and probably there were other people there too. Those were the people that I knew, but -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The name of his son that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know. That was Dzevad Besic, the father, and then his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were in Kozarac you told the court yesterday that you recognised, amongst the police and soldiers wearing camouflage uniform, someone you described as Gavro's son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is Gavro's son called Milos Gajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Otherwise known as -- or do you know him by another name, a nickname of "Dusko" or "Dule"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to him as "Gavro's son". Did you know him well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About how old was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around, I think I am not sure at that time, but about 35 to 40 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He was dressed in camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like now to turn to a different matter and that concerns the time that you spent in Omarska. You also spent time in Keraterm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that time that you were in Keraterm and Omarska did you see a man called Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you also see with him someone known as Dule Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think Duca, his last name is Banovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Otherwise known as "Dusko Banovic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everyone called him "Duca".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or you knew him as "Dusko Banovic"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will have to put a statement to you, sir, if the court will give us a moment? I would like you to look at this document that was an interview at that took place in Germany on 30th March 1994 involving matters concerned with this court, and during which there was a criminal investigator from the German police as well as an interpreter who spoke to you in your own language. I would like you to look at this document and, most particularly, could you look at page 3? Thank you, Mr. Usher. (Document was handed to the witness)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is your next exhibit number, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D19. That will be marked for identification purposes as D19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Does the Prosecutor have a copy of that, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not know whether they do or not; as it comes from the German papers, I imagine they do, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you provided with them with a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is the Serbo-Croatian translation of the German statement? We do have that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. MR. KAY (To the witness): Can you see that statement there in front of you which is a record of an interview that took place with you on 30th March 1994? Can you see that, Mr. Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I want to take you quickly to page 3. You see at the top of the page you mention names, Zoran Zigic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Dusko Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Spelt D-U-S-K-O?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my text, in our language it says "Dusko".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, not Duca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Banovic is a neighbour of my sister-in-law. This is where he comes from. I did not know Duca before. I could not have known his name or his last name. Everybody called him "Duca". When later I came out and during the camp I found out, I am not sure exactly at what time, so later I found out that that was Dusko Banovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You knew he was a waiter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you turn over the next page, page 4, do you see the name repeated there again or is it elsewhere on page 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are names on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You mention the name Dusko Banovic more than once; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible, that is likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Even further on in that statement towards the end on a later page, you again refer to him as being someone you knew as a waiter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that he was a waiter, and I put that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have referred to someone as "Duce"; by "Duce" you mean someone else entirely, do you not, someone known as Duca Knezovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Duca was, I am not sure about Duca, but he was from Orlovci, I know that, because he knew many people from Kozarusa itself. He beat personally Fajzo from Kozarusa and many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Dusko Banovic was someone that you saw in Omarska as well as Keraterm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Duca in Keraterm almost daily; in Omarska, I do not remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Dusko Banovic you also saw in Omarska, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if Mr. Bos could be so kind to collect D18 from the witness so that I may turn it to the appropriate page -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it is D19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: D19. Perhaps you would like to look at the seventh and eighth lines down, in fact, the second reference to Dusko Banovic on that page?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, what page are we on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 2 ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- or page 3, second page of the statement. (To the witness): Does it not say in there -- perhaps you can read out that whole passage that deals with Omarska and Dusko Banovic? Can you read it out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say it aloud. However, I was told that that night when my brother was in the white house Dusko Banovic and Zoran Zigic were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "They were beating the prisoners. Banovic and Zigic used to come to Omarska. They did not belong to any regular guard".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So in that passage there you do refer to Dusko Banovic going to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I pointed out that I had been told that people were seen when they would come and I saw Zigic with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was a statement that was signed by you in Germany for criminal proceedings that were starting in that country? You made that statement for the court, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. One other matter I would like to question you about in relation to your time at Omarska, and that concerns your knowledge of the days of the week and dates. Did you have any way of keeping track of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I arrived in Omarska camp, I arrived, I think it was the 8th, I also believe it was a Monday. I was first in room 15. I was not taken for interrogation, and it was only during the second week when they took me for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You said that you think you arrived in Omarska on what you believed was 8th June and you believed was a Monday. Did you have any way of knowing that those were the dates at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the day of my arrival, since the first day, since first day in the camp, I went first to Keraterm. I spent seven days in Keraterm and then I was taken away to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But the question that I asked was did you have any way of knowing what those days and dates were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could recognise all days and week and the exact date, well, some perhaps knew them, some perhaps did not, but we knew which day of the week, every day of the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand you say that, so was it because others told you what day of the week and what the date was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was taken for interrogation at 10 o'clock on Saturday morning. I was interrogated until 12 o'clock because in Omarska inspectors worked until noon, until 12 o'clock, on Saturdays and I was told that we would go on on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand you saying there that you were told that you would go on Monday, was that for a second interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Monday was the second day of the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you told that it was Saturday that you were first interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not say it was Saturday. We knew, all of us in Omarska knew, when inspectors came and when they went back, on which days they work and on which they did not, and Saturday, on Saturdays, they only worked until 12 o'clock, until noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Excuse me just for a moment. In that statement that I just put before you and before that passage concerning Dusko Banovic and Zoran Zigic, so it will be on the second page, if you turn it over, you will see that you were told that your brother had been beaten up and that you said in 1994 that you saw the body of your brother on a Saturday, on the meadow in the camp? Would you like to look at your statement on the previous page and just to see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see that, but it is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could read out that part so that we can check the language as against what has been written down there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can read it out, but on 20th June I could not see Smajo Kahrimanovic because I was interrogated on Monday, and that was the first time when I moved from the pista to restaurant to sleep there. Do you want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just read out the passage that it says, "I then could see on Saturday that the body of my brother was on the meadow in the camp".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "On Saturday, which was June 20th 1992, Smajo Kahrimanovic told me that my brother, Dalija, had died from injuries he sustained in the night between Friday and Saturday, and Saturday was the June 20th". So he was in the interrogation house for two days or, rather, in the glass house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You go on to say, do you not, that you could see on the Saturday the body of your brother on the meadow in the camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it say that here? That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, what I want to ask you about is this, whether dates and days that you have been giving are, in fact, your own recollection or because others have been speaking to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The days of the week I knew and I learned subsequently which dates they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you had conversations with other witnesses about events in Omarska and the days or dates that things happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, very likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I take that that is really a "yes"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have those discussions been with other witnesses in this case whilst you have been waiting for this trial to take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have not been talking with other witnesses in the last few days -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With witnesses, I did talk to other witnesses. I was with witnesses, but we did not discuss this because those witnesses were not there at that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all I ask. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Miss Hollis, do you have redirect?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, when you arrived here, you were informed that by court order you could not discuss this case with the witnesses or other persons other than the Prosecution or at this trial; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During these conversations that you had with other witnesses present here to testify, did you ever talk with them about this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have testified that your second interrogation occurred on a Monday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is your recollection of when that second interrogation occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you have also testified it was after this second interrogation that you were moved on to the pista; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you moved on to the pista then you slept at night in the restaurant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was it after you had been moved on to the pista that you were informed of your brother's death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you when you were informed of your brother's death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it who informed you of your brother's death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Smajo Kahrimanovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In response to an earlier Defence question when you were asked about a prior statement and you were shown the Serbo-Croatian translation of the German statement, I believe you indicated that you were told by others that a Dusko Banovic had been in Omarska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you yourself never said that you had seen Dusko Banovic in Omarska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in any of the camps, either Trnopolje, Keraterm or Omarska, did you know of a Dusko Banovic who was also referred to as "Duca"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you told this by other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody called him "Duca" and I learnt later on that his name was Dusko Banovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this person that was pointed out to you as Duca, you were later told was Duca Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Dusko Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not before the war.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your knowledge of him was when people pointed him out as "Duca" and then later told you he was Dusko Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The man that you saw when you were on the pista, the man that you identified in this courtroom as Dule Tadic, was that man the man who had been pointed out to you as "Duca"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated earlier in response to another Defence question that you could travel to Prijedor until 22nd May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then after 22nd May it was your understanding that Muslims could not travel from Kozarac to Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated also that when you would be at the checkpoint at Rajkovici that you would wear a camouflage hat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But that the hat was not a beret, is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not a real beret. They were caps that went along the clothes and it was also a camouflage colour, green, blue. It was multi-coloured like the clothes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, the day you were on the pista in Omarska camp and saw the man you have identified as Dule Tadic, is there any doubt in your mind that the man you recognised on that date is the Dule Tadic you have pointed to in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no doubt.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Whilst I am just dealing with the identification matter, perhaps the statement could be taken from the witness and handed back to Mr. Wladimiroff who will do some research for me?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, I have just a few more questions to deal with the occasion on which you say you saw Dusko Tadic on the camp at Omarska. At that time you were lying down on the pista; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was this in the month of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been June or July, early July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the time you were on the pista you were there with a large number of other prisoners; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you told the court yesterday, you were packed like sardines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was explaining we were lying next to each other in rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There were a lot of people out there on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, the pista was full of detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were over there towards the hangar, as you have indicated to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In answer to questions from counsel for the Prosecution, you told this court you did not have an unobstructed view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But, in fact, there were many other people lying down on the pista between you and the man you say was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were people, people were lying down on the pista, everybody was lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and a large number of people were between you and the man you say was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Was everyone lying down at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Between you and that man there were a large number of other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, who were lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The circumstances of your view was that you looked under your arm whilst your face was on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was down, my face was turned towards the white house, in the direction of the white house, so that I could see Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you were facing the white house, the position of the man you said was Mr. Tadic must have been at the end of your vision, on the side of your vision; you were not staring at him directly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see when I was down, I could see both the entrance into the building, who they were taking in, and also I could see the beating through the window. I could see how they were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But Mr. Tadic, you say, the man who was Tadic, was not by the white house; he was in another position altogether. He was down nearer the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have just told you when I would be lying down I could see whom they would be taking into the administrative building, and even I could look at the window, the one that you see on the model here, and the staircase. When we lied down, we would look under the arm or, perhaps, turn slightly, but lying like this, our head was always sideways so that you could see very many things; who was taken for interrogation, who was taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So would it be the case then that your arms were not by the side of your body, but positioned above your shoulders and that is how you come to look underneath your arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that I looked at Dule underneath my arm. I was like this. I was supporting myself like this and I was looking to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you said this morning was that you were on the pista mostly in a prone position, you would turn around and look under your arms and you can see what is happening when you look under your arms. That is what you told us earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so. That is what I said now. I do not really remember, but I think I have just said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said you were lying down on your stomach, you were looking towards the hangar, it was to the right, and you were looking at the glass of the white house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am just reading out what you said earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I believe there may be some confusion. There was a question about how this witness could see people being kicked or pushed down the stairs from the administration building if he was on the pista. He indicated that he would be in a position where he could sometimes look under his arms and see that window above A21, and that sometimes he would be in a seated position and could see that window above A21. I believe, however, that in response to my question he indicated that his face was turned to the right in the direction of the white house. I do not believe he specifically indicated in that portion of his testimony that he looked under his arm. If this is going to be a significant issue, I would ask that that portion of the transcript be provided so that the witness is not confused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, the transcript, of course, will show that. There have been so many questions about this first by Miss Hollis, then by you and then by Miss Hollis again and by you again, I think it is about time for it to come to an end really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted to deal with one other matter as I was going through what the witness said in answer to the questions of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you told counsel for the Prosecution was that no-one was blocking your view of Dusko Tadic as you were lying on the ground. That is not right, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is that in those circumstances you did not see Dusko Tadic at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know -- were you there or was I there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. There is one other matter, your Honour, and it is because we have not had an extra copy. I would like you to look at this document, please, again -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that Defence 19?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is D19, your Honour. You will see a passage in there dealing with your stay in Keraterm camp, can you see that. It is marked with pencil in brackets, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say in that statement, perhaps you can read it out, that passage, yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "During my stay in the camp at Keraterm, only men were brought to the camp, Muslims and Croats. Serbs soldiers gave us no food whatsoever, but our wives were allowed to bring us food which we then shared amongst ourselves. One could hear soldiers armed with automatic rifles. During the stay in the camp we were exposed to beatings. I know by name only Zoran Zigic and Dusko Banovic". Do you want me to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, just stop there. You said that you knew Dusko Banovic by name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the camp I knew only Zigic and Duca and I subsequently learned their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, it is your testimony that in the camp these two individuals were pointed out to you as Zigic and Duca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Subsequent to the camps, you were told that these individuals were Zoran Zigic and Dusko Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, at the time of giving this statement to the German investigators you had been told that these two men had those names; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you were on the pista and saw Dule Tadic, you indicated momentarily for the court the position that you were in. Would you please tell us at that time with your head facing to the right, did you have your head placed on your hands or were you looking under your shoulder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was resting on my hands like this, that I was lying like this.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other detainees who were lying on the pista in a prone position, did these other detainees block your view of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Hrnic, regarding Mr. Banovic: you testified that a gentleman who you were told to be Duca Banovic was pointed out to you while you were at Omarska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So you did not see a Duca Banovic at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Duca Banovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Duca in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How many times did you see Duca at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost daily, sometimes even several times a day.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: As I understand your testimony, you did not know him before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What did Mr. Banovic look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was very, very short, I do not know how, and he was very stolid, very sturdily built. He always wore a uniform. He was very well built. But he was not very tall, but he was of a normal height, a sort of wide-ish sort of person, that is, he was very sturdy.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, do you have additional questions in the light of my questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic, when you saw this man who was called Duca, did this man remind you of Dule Tadic or in your mind look like Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule was a big man but Duca was bigger.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever mistake Duca for Dule Tadic when you saw Duca in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not possible. Duca came daily to beat us down there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In your mind, were you clearly able to distinguish between the appearance of Duca and Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you have additional questions in the light of -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes, please. If we are finished with Mr. Hrnic, is there any objection to Mr. Hrnic being permanently excused? No objection? Mr. Hrnic, you are permanently excused. You may leave. Thank you for coming. (The witness withdrew) (11.30 a.m.) (The court adjourned for a short time) (11.50 a.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to that, your Honour, I had mentioned earlier that we were going to attempt to have a photograph made of the positions on the pista as marked by Mr. Hrnic. To my great amazement, it is possible. It has been done and we have a photograph. I have provided a copy of that to the Defence. I would ask that this be marked as the Prosecution exhibit next in line. It is a photograph showing the pista area with two yellow tabs, one with the letter "W" indicated by the witness to be where he was when he saw Dule Tadic, and with a yellow tab with the letter "T" indicating where the witness placed Dule Tadic at the time he saw him. Of course, for the court's orientation, I would note that the witness said he was close to the hangar building, and then the building to the other side of the pista would be the administration/restaurant building. I would offer this as the Prosecution exhibit next in line.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That should be 234. Any objection to 234?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I call Sulejman Besic. MR. SULEJMAN BESIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, would you take the oath there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is your full name Sulejman Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 25th April 1950.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you born, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Kozarac, village of Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how far is the village of Brdjani from the centre of Kozarac itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you live there all of your life up until 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived there all of my life up until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you attend your schooling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do eight years of school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then did you work for a period of time, approximately 10 years, as a lumberjack in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went into army in 1969 and I came back in 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Serbia, in the city of Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were doing your military service were you particularly trained in heavy artillery and in cannons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall when the war in Croatia commenced in the early part of 1991, I should say in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think this was around about the middle of 1991, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you still working at that stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As a chainsaw mechanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked in a lumber firm called Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did this firm have branches and offices and working places at various locations throughout the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you work in a number of places throughout opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But at all stages your home was in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When the war with Croatia commenced was there a call-up of people to join the army and go to the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did all members of the community respond to this draft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any particular section or segment of the community that did not respond to the draft that you knew of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One section, a smaller section, responded positively but most of the people did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did anything subsequently happen to the people who failed to respond to the draft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What occurred to people who did not respond to the draft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were mostly, they mostly lost their jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you yourself observe people in particular losing jobs in the employment in which you were engaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us the circumstances of how you came to see that happen and in respect of whom did it happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my company where I worked there were not a lot of bosses that were Muslims, there was just one that was Muslim, and he worked at assigning people to various tasks, and he was basically a head of that department; and at one point all of the old bosses that I knew when the war in Croatia started, they went somewhere, and then some new ones that I did not know came, but one of them I did know from before and his name was Gavran Bogdan and he said, "I am a new director and I will explain you some things that you have to know. You know that the war in Croatia started and it is our duty to protect Yugoslavia; you have to respond positively to the draft, all of you, and this is your duty. I also have a certificate that I got from a General", I forgot his name, and he showed us this certificate. There were about 50 of us in that room where we had a meeting with him, and there was a big seal there and he read that everybody who fails to respond to the draft will be fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "a big seal", was that the seal of the JNA, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, JNA, Yugoslav National Army, and underneath there there was a signature, I do not know who signed it, but it was signed by a General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did this then subsequently happen, that people who had failed to respond to the draft were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it happened to my boss who is the head of that department. He was fired after eight days and he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The people that were fired, were they then replaced by Serbs, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, new bosses came and then the simple workers, they felt, started feeling fear, and there were about half and half of us, half Muslims and half Serbs and Serbs started separating into separate groups in the canteen where we were eating or everywhere else. They did not really want to contact, to have any contact, with us. They were running away from us, and we, sort of, felt some kind of a fear. We watched on TV what was happening in Croatia. They were cursing Croatian President and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In May 1992, you were still working in this company yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not think that you had been drafted into the army; that was because of your age, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is the reason. One year before that, prior to that, I gave back my military uniform which I kept for 18 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In May were you working at a location the other side of the city of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you travel to that place to work from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was in May. I have to add that I before May 1st went to work and something happened. We would always go back from Bosanska Dubica every Friday, come back home, and on Monday we would go there, but something happened. We were in the forest. We were not informed, we were not informed that they did not allow us to go back home that Friday. Our boss told us that something was happening. The roads were closed and we had no opportunity to go back home. Around May 15th, they provided us with a transportation and we went from the place where we worked, we came to the road between Bosanska Dubica and Prijedor, and then I saw some military people there, who said machine guns from the left and to the right of the road; and they wanted us, to see our ID documents, and they were taking Muslims out and talk to them and then we could come back. So we had about three or four check points before, on the road to Prijedor; and when we came to Prijedor at one intersection, an intersection Prijedor/Kozarac, I saw many soldiers. I saw dust bags, I saw machine guns, and while the soldiers were checking us out at the intersection, I saw that they are speaking with a different dialect and they actually are not Bosnian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you able to determine the nationality of the soldiers from listening to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I recognised the dialect. Those were Serbs but Serbs from Serbia because they were using the term "bre".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. You said in your previous answer, at least it has been translated here, you say the soldiers that you saw at the intersection at Prijedor and Kozarac had "sawdust bags and machine guns".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Sand dust", "sand dust bags".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Sand dust bags, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with sand, with sand, filled with sand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You mean sand bags?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the Serbian soldiers that you saw appear to be regular JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not shaven, they were quite dirty. The uniforms that they had were quite dirty and they looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they have any distinguishing markings on them that you noticed, insignia of any sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed various insignia. I mostly noticed one person who was taking us out and checking our ID documents. He had some kind of sign on his sleeve. It looked like a bird, like an eagle. That is what I noticed on one soldier; and also I noticed insignia on their heads and those were kokardas which I had seen in the previous war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As you got closer to Kozarac, did you encounter another checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
